relatedSnapshot.title: TRPCError: You are not a member of this workspace.
Drop expected client TRPCErrors in Sentry beforeSend (noise reduction)
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

Several tRPC procedures intentionally throw `TRPCError` for **expected, fully-handled** conditions — entitlement/feature gates, auth guards, onboarding preconditions, and input validation. These are correct 4xx responses, not server defects, but `customBeforeSend` in `apps/web/instrumentation-server.ts` only *tags* them — and for Zod-validation errors it misses them entirely, because their message is a raw issues array that never contains the literal error code (the `exception.value.includes(code)` match at the tagging loop). As a result they are reported to Sentry as unhandled errors and dilute alert signal — ~14k events / 1,000+ user-instances across the issues below.

Surfaced by the `sentry-triage-shortlist` workflow (verify → prioritize → link-check). 0 real bugs; this is the top actionable noise-reduction theme.

## Fix

Extract the server `beforeSend` filtering into a unit-tested helper (`apps/web/lib/utils/sentry-trpc-filter.ts`) and:

* DROP a curated list of expected, fully-handled tRPC rejections (matched by message substring, each tied to its Sentry issue).
* Fix the validation-tagging gap so Zod input-validation TRPCErrors are tagged `error_type=client_error` and grouped under a stable fingerprint instead of one giant `TRPCError: [` bucket.
* Also fixes the previously-unreliable "not a member of this workspace" drop, which gated on the code string never present in the message.

## Sentry issues covered

* AI-CLIENTS-242 — BAD_REQUEST "Invalid organization id" (assertUserIsOrgMember)
* AI-CLIENTS-23C — PRECONDITION_FAILED NO_PROVIDER_CONNECTED (email-accounts onboarding)
* AI-CLIENTS-312 — FORBIDDEN feature-gate "… is not available"
* AI-CLIENTS-34M — FORBIDDEN RBAC "don't have permission to …"
* AI-CLIENTS-3NE — FORBIDDEN "Active subscription required …"
* AI-CLIENTS-17K — tRPC Zod validation array (tagged + grouped, not dropped)

Out of scope (follow-up): the AI-CLIENTS-34M client-side `enabled` gate so sdr/closer roles stop firing the guaranteed-403 query.

Stop AI SDR follow-ups once a prospect books through any tool
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

This is part 1 of ENG-14785. It stops every follow-up the moment a prospect has booked, however they booked. We need it first, because the other two children send prospects off to book outside our own slot finder. A follow-up after a booking shows a machine is writing.

## Problem

* We already watch the host's Name 4 or Outlook calendar, and a prospect's booking there cancelled 158 follow-ups in the 28 days to 6 Oct 2026.
* But a booking only counts when Company Two or EmailBison also marked the lead "interested". In a sample of 2,000 replied AI SDR threads, 94% had that mark, so about 6% of bookings are missed today. So is any sending tool that never sends the mark.
* A follow-up that's due between the booking and the calendar update still sends.

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Event on host calendar] --> B[CHANGED: prospect replied to us?]
  B -- yes --> C[Follow-ups cancelled]
  D[Follow-up is due] --> E[NEW: live calendar check]
  E -- booking found --> C
  E -- none found --> F[Follow-up sends]
```

The match rule changes, and a new check runs right before every follow-up sends.

## What's included

1. **Match on our own data.** A calendar guest counts as a prospect booking when either:
   * the existing Company Two or EmailBison evidence is there;
   * or the prospect sent at least one real reply, not an auto-reply, in an AI SDR thread in this workspace.

   Any reply counts: interested, question, objection or not now.
2. **A check right before each follow-up sends.** It looks for:
   * our own appointments for this prospect;
   * tracked external bookings for this prospect;
   * the host's connected calendar for the next 60 days.

   A booking counts if it was made after our first reply in the thread. The prospect, or another guest from the same company email domain, must be on it. Shared mail domains never count: gmail.com, outlook.com, <domain>, <domain> and similar.
3. **If the calendar can't be reached,** log it and send anyway, so a calendar outage never blocks follow-ups.
4. **Log which check stopped each follow-up,** so we can see how much each part helps.

## Out of scope

* Sending the host's own booking link: ENG-14788.
* Calendly's own booking messages, which are covered by a separate Calendly integration.

## Done when

* A prospect who books through any tool on the host's connected calendar has every pending follow-up cancelled, even when the sending tool never marked them "interested". How to check: an integration test, plus one run in preview.
* A follow-up due 1 minute after a booking lands is cancelled, not sent. How to check: an integration test.
* A guest from the prospect's company domain cancels follow-ups, and a gmail.com guest doesn't. How to check: unit tests.
* If the calendar lookup fails, the follow-up still sends and the failure is logged.

## Implementation context

* Detection rule: `handleExternalBooking` and `getQualifyingExternalBookingLeads` in calendar-sync-service.ts. Look at the evidence query around lines 2369 to 2433.
* Pre-send check: `validateFollowupExecution` in followup-validator.ts. It only knows about appointments already linked to the thread today.
* Synced calendar events don't store guests, so the check calls the calendar live. For Outlook, add guests to the fields we read.
* Full detail: AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Build the filter groups UI: all, any, and none matching with nesting
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Context.** Glossary: master ticket ENG-12174. For THIS ticket: our filter bar is a flat list where every condition is ANDed. Real sales lists need brackets: "match ALL of these, and NONE of those", with groups inside groups. The surprising part: the entire backend for this already exists (tables, recursive schema, the SQL builder, versioning); it has simply never been given a UI, and the list endpoints never accept groups as input. So this ticket is UI + plumbing on top of finished server code. The benchmark is the Hunter List, our SDR team's real 10,770-contact dial list in Close, which cannot be expressed without groups (its shape is written into the acceptance criteria as a test fixture). Why it matters: without groups, the team's most important list literally cannot be built here.

**Size:** M/L · **Design:** needed (extends the existing filter bar; Name 5 CRM page) · **Blocked by:** nothing
**How it should work (Close reference):** Match all/any/none and wrap-in-a-group: <url>
**Audit evidence:** ENG-12178 findings, "Nested groups" row. Real-usage proof: our team's Hunter List (the 10,770-contact SDR dial list) is built from nested groups with none-of matching and cannot be expressed in our flat AND-only filter bar.

### Overview

Reps can build filters like "match ALL of these, ANY of those, and NONE of the following", with groups inside groups. Example from our own Close workspace: leads with some communication AND status not Customer AND local time 8am-8pm, AND no meeting in the last 14 days, AND none scheduled in the next 30. Today our filter bar is a flat list that ANDs everything.

### Problem

The backend is completely built and persisted: `crm_filter_group` with nesting and and/or logic, the recursive input schema, `buildWhereFromFilterGroups` in the query builder, versioning, duplication, restore. But no UI component builds or edits groups, and no list procedure accepts `filterGroups` as input (they only take flat `advancedFilterRules`). Groups are dead code end to end. There is also no "none" mode, only and/or.

### Solution

* Group UI in the filter bar: wrap-in-group, per-group match mode (all / any / none), nesting one level minimum (match Close's practical depth), readable chip rendering of grouped filters.
* Thread `filterGroups` through the list procedures for contacts, companies, and deals (list + kanban + counts + export), reusing the existing builder.
* Add none-of semantics (negate a group) to the builder and schema if truly absent, or map "none" to NOT(any).
* Saved views persist and reload groups (already supported server-side).

### Scope

* In: group building/editing UI, chips rendering, list-procedure input plumbing, none-mode, persistence round-trip, tests incl. the Hunter List shape as a fixture.
* Out of scope: task/appointment surfaces, new field types, AI emitting groups (a follow-up once stable).

### Acceptance criteria

1. A rep can build: group A (match all) + group B (match none) with nested conditions, see it as readable chips, and the result set is correct on a fixture org.
2. The Hunter List shape (communication some AND status not X AND two recency exclusions and one future-window exclusion) is expressible and returns correct rows.
3. Groups save into a view, reload intact, and survive edit and re-save.
4. Flat existing views are untouched and continue to work; a flat view can be upgraded by wrapping rules in a group.
5. List, kanban, counts, and export all respect groups identically.

### Design (Name 5)

* 32 · smart view edit filters — the base filter editor. Note: the frame shows the flat AND rule list only; there is **no dedicated nested-groups mockup** — the all/any/none nesting extends this modal's pattern (sanity-check against Close's Smart Views screenshots linked on the master).

Full screen map on master ENG-12174.

relatedSnapshot.title: Run the power dialler on each lead's record, from any smart view
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What we want

A rep opens any smart view on People, presses **Power dialler** and works the list one person at a time, on each person's own record. The call sits in a bar at the top, the person's context fills the page under it, and the outcomes stay in the same place on the right. Anyone can add six ready-made calling lists, such as New leads and No-shows, from New smart view in one click: for themselves, or for the whole team if they're an admin.

Clickable designs: Power dialler designs (15 Oct 2026). Use the State menu at the bottom right to step through every state; add `&role=member` to a link to see what a non-admin sees, or `&amd=on` for answer detection on. It's private until James shares it from the page's Share menu.

## Why

Part of ENG-15216: this is where reps start and run a session.

* This replaces the Calling page this ticket used to describe. James reviewed the designs on 15 Oct 2026 and chose no separate page: reps should see each lead's full context as they're dialled, the way Close does, and starting from a smart view has to be obvious.
* Today the session is a card on the People or Deals list, so a rep in a session never sees the record of the person they're calling. Aaron's ENG-15235 asks for the profile to open when a call connects, and this delivers that outcome.
* Starting is hard today: 14 of 16 team People views can't start the dialler at all (ENG-15236), which is why that ticket blocks this one.
* No-shows were the busiest list in the 30 days to 12 Oct 2026, with 3,957 calls against 2,541 for booked calls, but reps have to build a view by hand to work them.
* ENG-15217 shipped on 14 Oct 2026 (outcome gate, 1.5 s Undo, keys, Skip, honest voicemail wording). This ticket moves those behaviours onto the record and restyles them; it doesn't rebuild them.

## How it should work

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Today
    A[Saved view on People or Deals] --> B[Start] --> C[Session card on the list]
    C -. rep opens the record .-> D[Session card is gone]
  end
  subgraph After
    E[Any smart view, or an added calling list] --> F[Power dialler 34] --> G[Person's own record: call bar, brief, outcomes]
    G -- outcome saved, 1.5 s Undo --> H[Next person's record, already loaded]
    G -- End session --> I[Session summary]
  end
```

### People, any smart view

* The button reads **Power dialler** with the number of callable people in a green pill ("Power dialler 34"). Hovering says "Calls the 34 people in Qualified this month one after another. Each person's brief opens before they pick up." On a phone it shrinks to the icon and count.
* The arrow next to it opens: **Continue calling** ("From Name 101, 7 of 34. Stopped at 11:40 am."), **Start from scratch**, and **Settings for this session**.
* Settings for this session holds Ring twice, a line saying whether answer detection is on or off and what a voicemail will do (linking to Phone settings), Caller ID, and the ring time. The ring time shown is the session's real setting (32 s by default), not a fixed number.
* When the view can't be called, the button is disabled with the reason and a fix link, as ENG-15217 already does.

### New smart view, Calling lists tab

* New smart view gets a third tab next to AI view and Manual filters: **Calling lists** (People, for everyone). Going back is one click on AI view.
* Above the cards, **Add as Personal or Team**. Everyone can add a list as Personal, which only they see. Admins can also pick Team, which everyone on the team sees in Views. Members see Personal only, with "Admins can add lists for the whole team."
* The AI view's empty state shows "Or start from a ready-made calling list" with the three busiest lists and a "See all six calling lists" link. The left column has the same link under its own heading, and the Views menu keeps "Calling list · ready-made".
* Six cards: New leads, Due now, No-shows, Missed calls, Unconfirmed and Today's calls. Each says who is in it and in what order, the live count, and the oldest wait. **Add** creates a normal view (Personal or Team) and opens it, so Power dialler dials it. A list that's already added reads "Added · Open".
* Footer: "A list skips anyone another rep is on the phone with, anyone marked Do not contact and anyone without a phone."
* The lists' rules run on the server, because some aren't filters (a missed inbound call, no reply to a confirmation text). Missed calls reads the missed inbound calls that ENG-12494 surfaces.
* **Exits:** Do not call, Wrong number, Not interested, Lost and Closed remove a person from every list. Missed calls exits on any connected outbound call or a Called back outcome. No-shows exits on Rebooked, Lost or a new appointment.
* **One eligibility time per person,** checked when claimed and when dialled, so switching lists can't get round the team-wide 60-minute redial gap.

### The session, on the person's record

* **Session strip** (one slim row): the view and position ("Qualified this month, 7 of 34") with a progress line, then Calls, Connected and rate, Booked, Talk and Session time, Up next, the keys list and an outlined **End session**.
* **Call bar:** the one coloured thing on the page. It's white in the preview and wrap-up, and pale green only while ringing or live. It shows the name large, company and title, their local time, phone, attempt, status in words ("Name 6 in 3 s", "No answer, ringing again (2 of 2)"), the timer, and the controls: Mute, Drop voicemail (V), Pause after this one, and a red hang up. While a call is live and recording is on, a **Recording** label with a red dot sits at the top of the session.
* **Under the bar:** the lead brief (ENG-15465), with the Activity and Details tabs one click away.
* **Right column:** the outcome panel, always in the same place. Before a call it's disabled with "Outcomes open when Name 7 picks up". Under it, a **Next up** card for the person after this one.
* A 3-second preview before each dial. Today's calls is preview only: the rep starts each call.
* Moving on opens the next person's record, which is loaded before the current call ends, so there's no wait.
* No black in the session: Call now, Next now and Resume are soft green, End session is outlined, hang up is red.

### End session

A summary: calls, connected and rate, booked, session time and talk time, and each person called with their outcome. **Keep calling** goes back to the session; closing returns to the view.

### Calling settings the session has to respect

Both cases of each setting must work. Values for our sales team's workspace are from the read-only replica on 15 Oct 2026.

| Setting | Our sales team today | When on | When off |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Answer detection (whole workspace) | Off | A machine answer hangs up before the beep, logs "Voicemail, no message", skips wrap-up and moves on. | The rep hears the voicemail and presses V or picks Voicemail. |
| Ring twice (per rep) | On for all 5 reps | Re-rings only when nobody picked up or the line was busy, never a voicemail. | One ring per person. |
| Automatic next call (per rep) | On, 5 s | The outcome gate and 1.5 s Undo from ENG-15217. | The rep presses Next (N). |
| Ring time (per session) | 32 s default | Shown in session settings as set. |  |
| Recording by default (workspace) | On | A Recording label shows while the call is live. | No label. |

Answer detection was on for 2,662 outbound calls in the 30 days to 15 Oct 2026: 1,390 came back as a machine, 503 as a person, and 769 had no clear answer, which the session treats as a person.

### Manager floor

Next to rep status, each calling list shows how many people are waiting and the oldest wait.

## Design

James approved these on 15 Oct 2026. Kit screens, light theme, 1440 wide:

 <image> 

The states after a call (waiting for an outcome, paused while typing, Next with Undo, keys, and voicemail with answer detection on and off) render in the new layout like this:

 <image> 

## Decisions already made

* No separate Calling page. A session always starts from a smart view or an added calling list.
* Calling lists are normal views. Anyone can add one as Personal; admins can also add one for the Team (James, 15 Oct 2026). They're renamed, pinned or deleted from Views like any other view.
* The session shows a Recording label while a recorded call is live (James, 15 Oct 2026).
* The button says Power dialler, whether the session is new or unfinished. Continue calling lives in its menu.
* The call bar is the only tinted surface, and it's green only while a call rings or is live.
* Ring twice never re-rings a voicemail, whether it was detected or heard.

## Not doing

* What's inside the lead brief: ENG-15465.
* What each outcome does after the call: ENG-15221.
* Attempt schedules and calling hours: ENG-15222.
* Leaving a recorded voicemail: ENG-12188.
* Fixing the views that can't start the dialler: ENG-15236.

## Open questions

* **Should** ENG-15235 **close once this ships?** Recommended: yes, because the record is on screen for every call in a session. Aaron and James decide.

## Done when

- [ ] From any team People view that passes the dialler preflight, Power dialler starts a session on the first person's record, with no extra setup.
- [ ] Each next person opens on their own record within a second of the Undo window closing, with the call bar and outcome panel in the same place.
- [ ] Adding a calling list from New smart view creates a view, Power dialler dials it, and the card then reads "Added · Open".
- [ ] A member can add a calling list only as Personal, and nobody else sees it. An admin can add one as Team, and every teammate sees it in Views.
- [ ] With default recording on, a live call shows the Recording label; with it off, no label shows.
- [ ] A person marked Do not call or Wrong number never appears in any calling list.
- [ ] A person called by anyone in the last 60 minutes isn't dialled from any list.
- [ ] With answer detection on, a machine answer logs "Voicemail, no message" and moves on. With it off, the rep hears the voicemail and can press V or pick Voicemail. A test covers both.
- [ ] Ring twice re-rings a no answer once and never re-rings a voicemail.
- [ ] End session shows the summary with counts that match the calls placed.
- [ ] The manager floor shows each calling list's oldest wait.
- [ ] PostHog receives `tool.opened` for the Calling lists tab and `dialler.session_started` with the view or list name.

<details><summary>For whoever builds it</summary>

* Code at commit 28fcbd9b55: the session card is `apps/web/components/crm-v2/phone/power-dialer-session-card.tsx`, mounted from `apps/web/components/crm/power-dialer/power-dialer-workspace.tsx`, which People (`people-table.tsx`) and Deals (`deals-kanban.tsx`) render. Moving the session onto the record means the record route owns it.
* Session summary already exists: `apps/web/lib/dialer/session-summary.ts` and `use-session-summary.ts` (calls and connected). Booked and talk time are new.
* Queue building: `apps/web/lib/dialer/materialize-queue.ts`. Detected voicemail skips wrap-up via `skipDetectedVoicemail` in `apps/web/lib/dialer/panel-state.ts`. Ring twice only re-rings NoAnswer and Busy (`apps/web/lib/dialer/ring-again.ts`).
* Settings: `voice_setting.answering_machine_detection_enabled`, `dialer_user_preference` (`auto_advance_enabled`, `auto_advance_seconds`, `ring_twice_enabled`), `dialer_session.ring_timeout_sec`.
* The design kit lives in the private frontend library (branch `power-dialler-design-2026-10-12`, commits up to `c0eaa80`). The screens are `crm-call-session.tsx`, `crm-call-queues.tsx` (Power dialler button and menu), `crm-calling-lists.tsx` (the six cards) and `crm-list-controls.tsx` (New smart view's Calling lists tab). Ask James for a walkthrough.
* Related: ENG-15159 (who last contacted a prospect), ENG-15237 (the call note on the profile).

</details>

relatedSnapshot.title: Prove which calling programs Twilio grants our workspaces, and cover the two calling workspaces now
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

This is the first step of ENG-15511. The two workspaces making 96% of our calls are non-US businesses, so we prove what Twilio will grant them before we build, and we get their numbers covered in the meantime.

## Problem

Draft checks (Evaluations) only prove that the fields pass Twilio's checker, not that Twilio will approve them. Twilio's docs don't say whether a non-US secondary profile can get a SHAKEN/STIR trust product. Voice Integrity asks for EIN or DUNS and a US address.

## What's included

**Part A: read and validate, with no submissions**

* **Parent account:** read its Trust Hub. Check whether the Primary Customer Profile is approved (Twilio blocks +1 calls without it), whether a parent SHAKEN/STIR product exists, and which numbers are assigned to it.
* **Policies:** `GET /v1/Policies`, to confirm the current SHAKEN/STIR, Voice Integrity and secondary-profile policy SIDs. Read them at runtime and never hard-code new ones.
* **Numbers:** for all 109 active numbers, record the account that owns each one and its existing Trust Hub assignments. The ENG-15511 decision on primary-account numbers needs this list.
* **Test subaccount:** create draft SHAKEN/STIR and Voice Integrity trust products and run Evaluations. Settle whether subaccount credentials or parent credentials work, and whether authorized representative 2 is required.
* **Today's attestation:** pull it from Voice Insights call summaries for 20 recent calls from each of the two calling workspaces.

**Part B: real submission for the two calling workspaces** (James approved this on 15 Oct 2026)

* **Before submitting:** set up an endpoint that saves the raw StatusCallback body, and test it.
* **Submit:** on each workspace's existing approved A2P secondary profile, submit a SHAKEN/STIR trust product. Also submit a Voice Integrity product where part A doesn't rule it out.
* **Assign numbers:** after approval, assign each workspace's existing subaccount calling numbers to the profile and to every approved product, and read each one back with GET.
* **Record SIDs:** record every account SID and product SID on this ticket, so ENG-15511's build adopts them and doesn't create duplicates.
* **Free Caller Registry:** submit the calling numbers to <domain>. It's free and covers all US numbers.

## Release rule

* Record eligibility separately for each program and each tested profile type (`CN`, `Other`).
* An explicit provider restriction (error 18609 or a documented rule) marks that program unsupported for that profile type.
* Any other rejection stays "unresolved" and gets one corrected resubmission.
* The build for a program starts once at least one profile type we serve is approved.

## Out of scope

* Transferring numbers between accounts: that waits on the ENG-15511 decision.
* Any app code: the attestation code is in its own child of ENG-15511, and the Settings flow is in a later child.

## Done when

* Every question above is recorded as VERIFIED or NOT VERIFIED, with its evidence.
* Each program has a recorded Twilio outcome (approved, rejected with reason, or still in review) for each of the two workspaces.
* The two workspaces' calling numbers on their subaccounts read back as assigned to every approved product.
* One raw StatusCallback body is saved, and its fields are listed.

## Implementation context

* The A2P helpers that create profiles, end users and trust products live under `lib/services/a2p-registration/brand/`.
* Run Twilio calls through `getSubaccountClient`.
* Policy constants are in `brand/shared.ts`. `RN806dd6cd…` there is the starter profile, not the primary profile.

relatedSnapshot.title: Refactor feature flags to be workspace-based
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

Feature flag access is currently controlled on a per-user basis. This makes rollout and permission management harder when a feature should be enabled consistently for everyone within the same workspace.

## Solution

Refactor feature flag evaluation and configuration so flags can be managed and resolved on a per-workspace basis instead of a per-user basis.

System-level roles must continue to retain their existing access behavior and should not lose access as part of this refactor. This includes roles such as customer success, closer, admin, and super admin.

## Scope

* Move feature flag targeting from user-level access to workspace-level access.
* Preserve existing system-level role access.
* Update the underlying implementation anywhere feature flags are read, stored, or enforced so workspace-based behavior is applied consistently.

## Permissions / ownership

* Workspace-based access should determine whether a feature is enabled for members of that workspace.
* System-level roles continue to have their existing access regardless of the workspace-based change.

## Acceptance criteria

* Feature flags can be enabled and evaluated at the workspace level.
* A user in a workspace with a given feature enabled receives access based on that workspace setting rather than a user-specific setting.
* Existing system-level roles, including customer success, closer, admin, and super admin, retain their current access.
* Existing feature flag checks no longer depend on per-user flag assignment for cases that should now be workspace-based.
* The refactor does not regress access for current internal operators with system-level roles.

## Open questions or design follow-ups

* Which system-level roles should bypass workspace-level gating entirely versus being granted access through a separate override path?
* Should per-user flag assignments be migrated, ignored, or removed after the workspace-based model is introduced?
* If a user belongs to multiple workspaces, which workspace context should be used for flag evaluation in each product surface?
* Is there any auditability or admin visibility requirement for who changed workspace-level feature flag settings?
* Are there any flags that must remain user-scoped, or should this refactor apply to all existing feature flags?

## Outcome

Feature access is managed primarily at the workspace level, while privileged system-level roles continue to work as they do today.

relatedSnapshot.title: Save reusable SMS templates in the workspace
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Give CRM somewhere to keep a reusable text message. This ticket adds the saved template itself and the rules for reading and writing one, so the later settings screen and the composer picker both have a single place to work from.

## Problem

CRM has reusable email templates but nothing equivalent for texts. There is no record of a saved text message anywhere, so no screen can list one and no composer can insert one.

## Proposed fix

Add a saved SMS template that belongs to a workspace, carries a name and a plain-text message, and can be listed, searched, created, renamed, edited and deleted under the same rules email templates already follow. Also record when each person last used each template, so the picker built later can offer their recent ones first.

Nothing user-visible ships in this ticket. It is the foundation the other two build on.

## What's included

* A saved SMS template with a name and a plain-text message.
* A record of when each person last used each template.
* List with search, read one, create, rename, edit, delete, delete several at once, and mark used.
* Workspace scoping on every read and write.
* Names unique within a workspace, ignoring letter case.
* Message length capped to what a text can actually carry.
* Deletion that keeps the record rather than destroying it.
* One shared way for the screens built later to read and change templates, so neither of them has to depend on the other.
* Preview environments seeded with this data.

Not included: any screen, the composer picker, placeholder handling, sharing beyond the existing email-template rules, folders or categories, and default seeded templates.

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately.

## How it should work

* A template belongs to one workspace and is visible to everyone in it.
* A name already used in that workspace is refused, and a difference in letter case is not a way around it.
* The message is capped at the same length the existing texting routes enforce, so a template can never hold a message that cannot be sent.
* Deleting marks the template deleted and records who did it. Deleted templates disappear from every list and cannot be read, renamed or deleted again.
* Deleting several at once refuses the whole request if any one of them is missing or not that person's to delete, rather than partly succeeding.
* Marking a template used records the moment for that person only, and repeating it updates the existing record rather than adding another.
* A request naming a template in another workspace is refused and changes nothing.

## Who can do what

Anyone in the workspace who can send a text can list, read, create one, and record that they used one. Renaming, editing and deleting are limited to whoever created the template, plus workspace owners and admins. Nobody can reach a template in another workspace.

These are the rules email templates follow, with one deliberate difference: recording a use is treated as a write here rather than as a read. A client role cannot send a text at all, so recording that it used a template would be a write with nothing behind it. Email has no equivalent restriction because its send route does not have one.

## What the user sees

Not applicable: this ticket ships no user-visible surface. Its behavior becomes visible through the settings screen and the composer picker that follow it.

## Done when

- [ ] A template can be created, listed, searched, read, renamed, edited and deleted.
- [ ] Two templates in the same workspace cannot share a name, including when only letter case differs.
- [ ] A message longer than a text can carry is refused.
- [ ] A deleted template is absent from every read and cannot be changed again.
- [ ] Deleting several at once either does all of them or none.
- [ ] Someone from another workspace is refused and nothing is written.
- [ ] Only the creator, an owner or an admin can rename, edit or delete.
- [ ] Marking used keeps one record per person per template and updates it on repeat.
- [ ] Preview environments contain this data without leaving broken references.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

A saved SMS template exists as real, workspace-scoped, permission-checked data, so the settings screen and the composer picker can each be built without inventing storage of their own.

## Implementation context

* Mirror the completed email template implementation rather than designing a second template system. It already settles naming rules, soft deletion, the recent-use record and the permission split.
* The message cap must match the limit the existing send and schedule routes enforce, not the far larger email body limit, so a template can never be saved that those routes would then refuse.
* A new table needs both its preview-dump entry and orphan cleanup for any foreign key pointing into a table that is only partly copied. Nothing in CI catches that omission.
* Wider background for this work is in the AI context.md on the parent ticket.

Deliver each Gmail notification to every switched-on workspace
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a rep has switched their Gmail inbox on in more than one workspace, each new email should appear in all of them on its own. Today Gmail's live notifications reach only one workspace.

## Problem

Gmail allows only one live watch per mailbox address, and our record of that watch belongs to a single workspace binding. Notifications therefore resolve to one workspace. Switching a second workspace on would even take the watch away from the first, and switching off the workspace that owns the watch record would silence the rest.

## Proposed fix

Make the watch record belong to the mailbox instead of one workspace, and keep exactly one live watch per mailbox address. On each notification, read Gmail's new history once and save it into every workspace whose binding is currently active, each with its own progress.

## What's included

Included: the watch record serving every active workspace of the mailbox; notifications resolving to all active workspaces; one history read written into each workspace with its own progress; failure isolation between workspaces; no writes to a switched-off workspace; the watch stopping only when no active workspace remains; rebaseline and watch renewal acting on all active workspaces.

Excluded: Outlook (live sync for it is still to be built, see Keep Microsoft 365 conversations up to date automatically), the settings switch (Show a per-workspace Email sync switch in Email & Calendar settings), the binding change already delivered in Let one connected mailbox hold an active binding in more than one workspace, and any change to which mail is saved.

## Blocked by

* Track Gmail live sync progress separately for each workspace

## How it should work

* One watch per mailbox address, as today. A notification reads Gmail history once, starting from the oldest workspace position, and saves into each active workspace that has not already passed that point.
* Each workspace's progress moves only after its own save commits. If one workspace's save fails, only its progress stays put and it retries on its own. The others advance normally.
* Switching a second workspace on joins the existing watch and does not take it from the first. The first keeps syncing without interruption.
* Switching one workspace off stops writes there and leaves the watch for the others. The watch stops only when the last active workspace is switched off, the rep leaves it, or the mailbox is disconnected.
* A workspace whose progress is too old to continue is recovered on its own with the same bounded re-scan as today, without pausing the others. Renewal keeps the one watch alive while any workspace is active.

## Who can do what

Unchanged: only an active workspace binding may read or write that workspace's copy of the mailbox's CRM data. A switched-off workspace receives nothing, exactly as if it were disconnected.

## What the user sees

A rep with Email sync on in two workspaces sees new incoming and sent Gmail mail appear in both, without opening a page or doing anything. A switched-off workspace gets no new mail and keeps its existing history. Nothing else about Gmail changes.

## Done when

- [ ] A rep with Email sync on in two workspaces sees new incoming and sent Gmail mail arrive in both without further action.
- [ ] One Gmail notification gives each active workspace its own independent progress.
- [ ] A failed save in one workspace does not block or corrupt another workspace's progress, and it retries on its own.
- [ ] A switched-off workspace receives no writes.
- [ ] Switching a second workspace on does not take the watch from the first, and switching one off does not stop mail for the rest.
- [ ] Only one live watch exists per mailbox address at any time.
- [ ] Watch renewal and rebaseline work for a mailbox with more than one active workspace.
- [ ] Live QA on Gmail covers two workspaces on, one switched off mid-flow, and a rebaseline while more than one is active.

## Open questions

* When one workspace needs recovery and another is fine, what does the mailbox show? Recommended default: keep the watch live for everyone and record the recovery need only on the affected workspace.

## Expected outcome

"New mail arrives in every switched-on workspace without any further action" becomes true for Gmail, and the settings switch delivers ongoing sync, not just a one-time import.

## Implementation context

* Part of Fan Gmail live sync out to every workspace an inbox is switched on in.
* Expand then contract: keep the old per-workspace key and its unique index in this change, and drop them only in a later cleanup, so the app version still running during a deploy stays safe.
* Preview cannot plant Gmail webhooks. Live QA needs the live Gmail QA workspace recipe used for Bring new Gmail mail into CRM as it arrives and Recover Gmail sync on its own after stale history, lost access or deleted mail.
* AI context: AI context.md
